rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3 and Table 1 - a two-year (2018-2019) pot experiment in a greenhouse at Jiangxi Academy of Agricultural Sciences with four treatments (CK running water, LM, MM, HM micro-nano bubble water) on early and late rice, reporting own measurements of yield, yield components, tillers, SPAD, Pn, roots, biomass and nitrogen.
rows.notes: The study is primary but tests micro-nano bubble (MNB) oxygenated water added to flooded pots every 5 days (water poured by graduated container), not drip irrigation; the claim row is tagged technology = drip. The 14.31% figure cited in the passage is indeed the study's own result (Table 1: HM late rice +14.31% over CK in 2018; early rice +4.84~10.95%), so the review correctly reports the MNB yield effect, but the delivery technology is pot flooding, not drip. If the claim were read as MNB irrigation generally, the study would support Q2 (yield increase), Q4 (soil-solution dissolved oxygen, root traits, SPAD/Pn measured as intermediate variables, Figure 1, Table 2, Figure 2), Q8 (Section 4.2: ideal greenhouse pot conditions without rain, air-source generator limited to 1000 mL/min, extension to field needs further study) and Q9 (Table 1 reports means <U+00B1> SD/SE for grain yield); but not Q3 (single method), Q5 (one site/soil, two rice seasons only), Q6 (pots) or Q7 (no stated requirement condition).

notes: Full text available; some pages have garbled overlapping text from PDF extraction (page 3 Methods) but content is recoverable. Study is a greenhouse pot experiment with MNB water applied to flooded pots, not drip irrigation.
